newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS NETS NEW HAUL AS AMERICAN EXPRESS SPOKESMAN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS NETS NEW HAUL AS AMERICAN EXPRESS SPOKESMAN.

text.p: Tiger Woods reeled in another huge prize, this time off the golf course, on Monday as the American Express Co. announced an agreement making the 21-year-old golf sensation a worldwide spokesman.

Terms for the multi-year agreement with the financial services company were not disclosed but reports are putting the fee as high as $30 million for five years to feature Woods in advertisements for various American Express products.
As part of the deal, which has been in the works since December, American Express said it contributed $1 million to the Tiger Woods Foundation, which aims to introduce golf to inner city youngsters.

Woods, whose popularity has so transcended the sport that he was dubbed by a New York Times columnist as "golf's Beatle," continued his remarkable roll since turning pro last August by winning the Byron Nelson Classic Sunday in his first start in a month since his record-breaking Masters triumph.
The three-time U.S. Amateur champion earned $324,000 for his victory Sunday, pushing his nine-month-old career winnings past the $2 million mark faster than any golfer in history.

Woods, whose endorsement deals with Nike and Titleist allowed him to turn professional with $60 million already in pocket, said the American Express deal fits into his off-course strategy to control his own image.
"I have already established a brand plan as to who I am," said Woods, who chooses to work with companies where he will be "promoted correctly ... as to how I want to be perceived."
For American Express, that image is "global."

The California native of racially mixed parentage -- his father is black and mother is a native of Thailand -- called himself "an ethnically global person," and said he wanted to work with a global company.
Woods said other companies have asked him for his endorsement but he said he was concerned about how his "image is handled."

Woods became the first black to win a major golf championship when he won the Masters with a record low score and record winning margin as its youngest ever champion. He has played 16 events since turning pro and won five times.
